title: Affine sections of a localizing presheaf survive sheafification
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $P$ a presheaf of $\mathcal O_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume that for every affine open $W\subseteq T$ and every $a\in\Gamma(T,W)$, the restriction $P(W)\to P(D(a))$ is module localization at powers of $a$, with scalar action obtained by restriction from $\Gamma(T,W)$. Then for every affine open $W$, the component $P(W)\to P^\#(W)$ of the canonical module sheafification unit [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] is an isomorphism of $\Gamma(T,W)$-modules.

source.place: Tags 01HV and 009N/009Q (lemma-extend-off-basis, lemma-extend-off-basis-structures): principal-open localization and basis extension.

proof.text: For fixed W=Spec A and N=P(W), the localization hypotheses identify P(D(a)) with N[1/a]. Uniqueness of maps out of localization and presheaf naturality identify all further principal restrictions with those of tilde N. Thus the presheaf on the principal basis agrees with the associated module sheaf.

The principal-basis presheaf is a sheaf on that basis. Extend it uniquely by the sheaf-on-basis extension theorem. Its stalks and hence its associated sheaf agree with those of P restricted to W. The canonical unit induces the basis agreement. Since W=D(1), its component on W is an isomorphism. Sheafification commutes with restriction by its universal property and the same stalk description. This does not assume that T is separated.
